A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PORRL framework and retain matching algorithms and proofs. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, including v3's added figure and theoretical appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports mathematical guarantees, proofs, and analytic toy examples, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical throughout its main text and appendices. The new transition-model extensions and illustrative diagram do not report original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Appendix F adds general-transition variants of POR-UCRL and POR-UCBVI beyond v2's concrete tabular constructions. These introduce likelihood-based transition confidence sets and bonuses, with strong-SAIL variants executing additional exploratory policies. The original tabular procedures and GOLF remain.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or benchmarks. The additional function-approximation settings in v3 are theoretical model classes, not newly evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Neither version contains empirical baseline comparisons. KTO and DPO are added as motivating citations in v3, while OMLE supplies theoretical building blocks; these are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental splits, preprocessing, evaluation budgets, or testing protocols. Appendix F's exploratory-policy rules belong to proposed algorithms rather than conducted experiments.

E4.justification: Both retain analytic combination-lock and memoryless-policy examples. No empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or error analyses are added; the new hardness argument is theoretical.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, error bars, or significance tests. Their confidence sets and high-probability bounds concern theoretical algorithms, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version contains measured performance values, experimental rankings, or empirical result entries. The newly reported quantities are mathematical regret bounds.

T1.justification: New Appendix F introduces transition-complexity definitions, derivations, Theorems 10–12, and Corollary 6 for general function approximation. Proposition 1 and Appendix G.2.2 also add a claimed Omega(sqrt(A^H T)) sparse-feedback lower bound using a bandit argument. Assumption 1 changes the feedback mean from 'known' to 'unknown' and explicitly describes the Lipschitz constants as unknown.

C1.justification: The abstract's main contribution claims remain unchanged. v3 adds practical implications as an explicit contribution and advertises general transition-function approximation in the introduction, modestly broadening the stated contribution scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds practical guidance concerning actor-critic methods and strengthens the sparse-feedback interpretation to an algorithm-independent hardness claim. Appendix F adds substantive qualifications: strong-SAIL bounds exclude exploratory-policy regret, and the corresponding dueling extension requires a single exploratory policy. The shared-Q-network recommendation already appeared in v2.

D1.justification: Appendix F specifies technical setup for the new variants, including storing policy–trajectory pairs, recursive likelihood confidence-set updates, and a threshold beta defined using bracketing numbers and confidence level delta. Existing algorithms' technical descriptions are largely retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to KTO, DPO, and Xiong et al. (2024), removes several broad alignment and LLM references, and develops its relationship to the already-cited Liu et al. (2022b) for transition approximation. The central RLHF and POMDP positioning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and selected explanations receive targeted edits, and Section 5 gains practical-implication bullets. Inserting Appendix F shifts the former F/G appendices to G/H; most existing proof prose and the main narrative structure remain. Affiliation and senior-authorship text also change.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-panel Figure 1 illustrating cardinal and dueling feedback. It also widens the text area, adjusts spacing and page breaks, and relocates Algorithm 1 relative to the reduction theorem. Existing algorithm displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves exposition and supplies explicit general-transition extensions absent from v2. However, Theorems 11–12 explicitly omit exploratory-policy regret, and the new sparse-feedback lower bound invokes generic bandit bounds without clearly establishing their applicability to the restricted Bernoulli(q)/zero combination-lock construction in Appendix G.2.2. These unresolved scope and proof issues coexist with useful additions, preventing a reliable net judgment of overall quality.
